subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: Should an authenticated SMS callback that exceeds OpenClaw's dispatch quota be reported to Twilio as successfully processed even though OpenClaw intentionally discards it?
rationale: The choice determines the channel's delivery guarantee and whether provider retries and failure diagnostics remain available; tests cannot establish the intended product contract.

options.title: Require durable acceptance before 2xx
options.body: Revise the path so success is returned only after dispatch or durable queue admission, preserving a retry-visible failure otherwise.

options.title: Approve intentional ack-and-drop
options.body: Explicitly accept message loss, document its monitoring and retry consequences, and require exact-head live Twilio evidence before merge.

options.title: Pause for quota redesign
options.body: Hold or close this PR until the authenticated-callback quota can provide bounded backpressure without falsely acknowledging dropped messages.

recommendation.title: Require durable acceptance before 2xx
recommendation.body: Revise the path so success is returned only after dispatch or durable queue admission, preserving a retry-visible failure otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged quota implementation established the current callback-admission boundary that this decision would redefine.
